chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Habib al-Kha'thami, who said:
I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the frequent forgetfulness (distraction) in prayer, so he said, 'Count your prayer with pebbles,' or he said, 'Preserve it with peebbels.'

key_terms.الْحَصَى: Small pebbles or stones used for counting

ai.seo_question: How to overcome distraction during Islamic prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes using pebbles (*al-hasā*) as a tactile mnemonic device to counteract *sahw* (forgetfulness/distraction), a common challenge in ritual prayer. This practical advice underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on combining spiritual mindfulness (*khushu*) with physical aids to ensure the validity and completeness of the prayer units (*rak'at*). It reflects a holistic approach to worship where external tools support internal devotion.
